newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya postpones regional summit on Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Kenya postpones regional summit on Sudan.

text.p: Kenya has postponed a regional summit whose highlight would have been a face-to-face meeting between Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir and southern Sudan rebel leader John Garang, Kenya's Foreign Ministry said.

A ministry official said the meeting, under the regional Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGAD), had to be postponed because African officials were busy preparing for the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit in Harare next week.

Ugandan officials said last week that Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi, who chairs an IGAD sub-committee on Sudan comprising Kenya, Uganda, Eritrea and Ethiopia, was trying to bring together Garang and Lieutenant-General Bashir. Direct talks between the two are seen as key to peace in Sudan.

Garang's rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) has fought since 1983 for greater autonomy of the Christian and animist south from the Moslem, Arabised north and has launched a sewries of successful offensives this year.
Kenyan officials have been quiet about plans for face-to-face talks between the Garang and Bashir.

Moi hosted a meeting between Bashir and Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni on May 10 in a bid to resolve their differences. Moi said he wanted an amicable solution to their mutual problems because the region needed development instead of conflict.
Uganda accuses the Sudanese government of arming and giving bases in south Sudan to Ugandan rebels of the Lord's Resistance Army. Sudan accuses Uganda of arming and supporting the SPLA.
The Lord's Resistance Army has been severely weakened by the strength of the SPLA in the south but Garang denies he is fighting for Uganda.
Kenya's Foreign Ministry said it still did not know when the IGAD meeting on Sudan would be held, but it would come soon after the Harare OAU summit.
